newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-AJAX STRIDE ON TOWARDS LAST EIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AJAX STRIDE ON TOWARDS LAST EIGHT.

text.p: Ajax Amsterdam took a signifcant step towards the last eight of the European Cup when they overcame a weakened Glasgow Rangers 1-0 in their Champions' League group A match on Wednesday.
The only goal of a fiercely-contested game came after 39 minutes when midfielder Arnold Scholten scored his first goal in 35 European appearances.
He lashed home a low, powerful 25-metre drive which flew past the outstretched right arm of Rangers's Dutch goalkeeper Theo Snelders.
The defeat was Rangers fourth in succession, confirming their elimination with two matches to play.
Ajax, who have nine points from their four matches, were made to fight hard for their win and found Rangers a far tougher side to beat than the one they outclassed 4-1 in Amsterdam two weeks ago.

Rangers were without the suspended Paul Gascoigne, sent off in Amsterdam, skipper Richard Gough and defenders Alec Cleland and Craig Moore, but battled throughout, especially in the last half an hour and were a little unfortunate not to salvage a point.

Said Ajax manager Louis Van Gaal:: "We played very well in the first half and scored a very good goal but we became nonchalant after halftime and gave Rangers the initiative. Still, I think they only had one-and-a half chances to score."

Rangers manager Walter Smith said: "I was disappointed we didn't get more out of the game. They were the better team in the first half but we held our own in the second and had the better of the play."
In a sense Ajax's victory was sealed after Rangers' German midfielder Joerg Albertz blasted a six-metre shot high over the bar with only goalkeeper Edwin Van der Saar to beat after 59 minutes.
"I had too much time to think about it," said Albertz. "I think if I had scored then we could have gone on to win."
Rangers's only other real scoring opportunity came in the last minute when their second Dutchman, substitute Peter Van Vossen, fired narrowly wide across goal.
Rangers have now gone 12 Champions' League matches without a victory since the 1992-93 season.

Smith was forced to give a first team debut to 19-year-old defender Scott Wilson and also play inexperienced 20-year-old Greg Shields in a patched-up team which was missing six senior injured players as well as the four suspended men.

But the youngsters gave a good account of themselves against the Dutch champions, although they were lucky that dangerman Patrick Kluivert, just returning after a lengthy lay-off because of a knee injury, was ring rusty and not yet on top of his game.

They coped well with irrepressible Nigerian winger Tijani Babangida, who helped demolish Rangers two weeks ago, and with the combined driving force of twins Frank and Ronald de Boer, who orchestrated most of Ajax's moves before Frank went off with cramp 20 minutes from time.

Rangers - 13-Theo Snelders; 29-Scott Wilson (18-Erik Bo Andersen 85th), 5-Gordan Petric, 6-Joachim Bjorklund, 28-Greg Shields, 20-Derek McInnes (9-Ally McCoist 81st), 14-Ian Durrant, 3-Joerg Albertz, 16-Charlie Miller (17-Peter Van Vossen 59th), 15-David Robertson, 11-Brian Laudrup

Ajax - 1-Edwin van der Sar; 2-John Veldman, 4-Frank de Boer (16-Nordin Wooter 70th), 20-Marcio Santos, 29-Mario Melchiot, 6-Ronald de Boer, 8-Richard Witschge, 7-Tajani Babangida (21-Dani 72nd), 11-Marc Overmars (28-Rody Turpijn 79th), 19-Arnold Scholten, 9-Patrick Kluivert
